pattern.top_pattern: Rare catastrophic and transplant-related cases need individual case management, not broad policy changes
pattern.what_is_impacting: IN / TX / UNATTRIBUTED / VA / OH rare high-cost inpatient cases
key_driver_codes: ENC AFTERCARE FLW MX ORGN TRANSPL
Coronary Bypass without Cardiac Catheterization with MCC
Amputation for Circulatory System Disorders Except Upper Limb and Toe with MCC
pattern.pattern_details: This pattern is made up of one-off or very rare high-cost inpatient cases, including transplant aftercare, major cardiothoracic surgery, coronary bypass, amputation, and other severe episodes. Counts are very small, but the cost per case is high enough to create noticeable spend movement. These are best handled through individual case validation and large-case management, not through broad utilization policy changes.
pattern.why_it_matters: Rare outliers can distort trend signals and require stop-loss, case-management, and claim-validation responses instead of program-wide intervention.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Route these cases to clinical review and large-case management for claim-level validation, severity confirmation, and any applicable stop-loss or transplant case management follow-up.
pattern.validation_reason: The pattern is built from very small counts and low-baseline cases, so claim-level confirmation is needed before drawing broader conclusions.
evidence_summary: A single lung transplant aftercare admission added about +$0.4M.
Multi-organ transplant aftercare added about +$0.1M, and an aortic dissection case added about +$0.1M.
OH rare one-case episodes included about +$46K for coronary bypass and about +$45K for amputation related to diabetic gangrene.
